title: Moral Letters to Lucilius
author: Seneca
summary: An elderly Roman Stoic philosopher gives life advice to a young friend.
desc: Seneca was a Stoic philosopher and statesman in Rome’s early post-Augustan era. He was Nero’s tutor, and then his advisor when Nero became emperor in 54 CE. After Seneca retired from public life, he wrote a series of letters to his friend Lucilius, the procurator of Sicily. These letters were circulated right before Seneca’s death in 65 CE, when Nero forced him to commit suicide for his alleged involvement in a conspiracy. title: Robur the Conqueror
author: Jules Verne
summary: A domineering inventor kidnaps members of a balloonist club and flies them around the world to prove the superiority of his heavier-than-air machine.
desc: Robur the Conqueror , also published as The Clipper of the Clouds , opens in Philadelphia at a meeting of the Weldon Institute, a club of balloon enthusiasts. A stranger named Robur asks to address the members, then tells them that the future belongs to heavier-than-air machines. He mocks the club’s giant balloon, the Go-Ahead , and insults its members until the meeting erupts in chaos. title: Of One Blood
author: Pauline E. Hopkins
summary: A young scholar’s life spirals down a dark path after the near-death of a singer.
desc: Attending medical school in Boston, Reuel Briggs has neither wealth nor the good looks of the upper-class white society with which he surrounds himself. He is, however, incredibly talented, and has a rare gift in the psychological study of mysticism and supernatural phenomenon. Even if his peers aren’t too keen on him, they can’t help but be awed by his talent, and subsequently call on his aid in reaching out to the minds of the sick and dying who would otherwise be lost. title: The Sowers
author: Henry Seton Merriman
summary: Driven by their shared idealism, two men returning to Imperial Russia to effect change face mortal danger from both an autocratic state desperate to preserve its power and a peasantry driven to desperation by centuries of servitude.
desc: With The Sowers , a story ranging from the upper class drawing-rooms of London, Paris, and St. Petersburg to the vast estates and peasant villages of the Russian steppe, Henry Seton Merriman enjoyed his greatest popular success. title: Beautiful Stories from Shakespeare
author: E. Nesbit
summary: Children’s author E. Nesbit retells some of Shakespeare’s plays for young readers.
desc: Two young couples, lost in an enchanted wood, are manipulated by quarreling fairies. A magician and his daughter entertain visitors he shipwrecked on their enchanted island. A king divides his lands unequally among his three daughters according to how well they flatter him. A witches’ prophecy sets a Scottish general on a tragic path. title: The Storm of Steel
author: Ernst Jünger
summary: A German storm troop officer recounts his experiences in World War I.
desc: Ernst Jünger was a German officer commanding storm troopers during World War I. This, his memoir of his time on the front, is one of the very first literary accounts of the Great War. Jünger begins his story as a private entering training in the Champagne region. He continues on to take part in various battles, climbing the ranks until attaining command of a regiment and accumulating fourteen different hits from bullets or shrapnel. title: On the Making of Man
author: Gregory of Nyssa
summary: An early Christian theologian expounds on the doctrine of humanity being made in God’s image.
desc: On the Making of Man is an early treatise on theological anthropology, the area of Christian theology that inquires into human nature with respect to God. In the treatise, the 4th century bishop and theologian Gregory of Nyssa interprets the creation narrative found in the first three chapters of the Book of Genesis. title: Oberland
author: Dorothy M. Richardson
summary: An independent young woman from London is gifted a two week trip to a resort in Switzerland.
desc: Oberland is the ninth “chapter volume” of Dorothy M. Richardson’s pioneering semi-autobiographical series, Pilgrimage . Series protagonist Miriam Henderson spends two weeks at the Hotel Alpenstock, a resort in the the Bernese Oberland region of Switzerland, mainly in the company of other English guests. title: The House of the Arrow
author: A. E. W. Mason
summary: A blackmailer falsely accuses a dead woman’s niece of murder by poison, but the evidence suggests the accusation might not be false after all.
desc: After the apparently natural death of wealthy widow Madame Harlowe, a blackmailer accuses her niece of murder by poison—an accusation he knows to be false. The famous French detective Inspector Hanaud is called in, with Madame Harlowe’s death only an excuse to investigate a series of anonymous blackmailings the local police have been helpless to solve. title: Barlasch of the Guard
author: Henry Seton Merriman
summary: Caught between the empires of Napoleonic France and Tsarist Russia, those in Danzig struggle to survive a nightmare of occupation and destruction, but within this the unlikeliest of friendships offers salvation to two very different people.
desc: One of Henry Seton Merriman’s most popular and acclaimed novels, Barlasch of the Guard explores the ideals and imperfections of people, great and small alike, under the incomprehensible strains of life under siege, beset by the destructive forces of both man and nature. title: His Royal Nibs
author: Winnifred Eaton Reeve
summary: A young Englishman finds a new purpose in life as a hired hand at a ranch in Canada.
desc: A young man dubbed “Cheerio” for his English background, clean appearance, and well-kept suit, unexpectedly arrives at the highly regarded O Bar O ranch with one goal in mind: to offer his services as a hired hand, and thus find a new start in life in a foreign land. title: The Autobiography of a Super-Tramp
author: W. H. Davies
summary: At the end of the 19th century, a destitute tramp wanders across England and North America.
desc: The Autobiography of a Super-Tramp , poet W. H. Davies’ autobiography, recalls spurning a youth of subsistence and squalor in England to pursue a life of travel abroad. With quiet and understated prose, Davies recounts a tramp’s life: riding railroad boxcars and evading fare collectors, cadging free meals, working as a migrant field hand, and dealing with corrupt law enforcement and judges. title: Contending Forces
author: Pauline E. Hopkins
summary: A young woman of color reckons with her troubled past after she settles in Boston.
desc: In response to the upcoming abolition of slavery in the British Empire, Charles Montfort, an English planter in Bermuda, decides to move his family (and his human chattel) to the southern United States in order to free his slaves on his own schedule. title: Sentimental Education
author: Gustave Flaubert
summary: A young man in mid-19th-century Paris obsesses over a friend’s wife.
desc: The young Frederick Moreau sets out for Paris to start his career, holding a letter of recommendation to a banker and the address of a friend. But when his introduction is unsuccessful, he finds himself at the shop of the art dealer Jacques Arnoux, where he meets Arnoux’s wife. title: Reflections on the Revolution in France
author: Edmund Burke
summary: The conservative political theorist Edmund Burke critiques the political program of the French Revolution.
desc: Written in 1790 during the early stages of the French Revolution, Reflections on the Revolution in France is regarded as one of the foundational texts of conservative political theory.
